# GoCD Lens

> A browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave) that reads GoCD pipelines from the GoCD REST API and
> draws its own dashboard, so it keeps working when the GoCD web UI does not. Everything it stores
> stays on the user's machine; the only host it contacts is the user's own GoCD server.

GoCD Lens is free and MIT licensed. It is not affiliated with the GoCD project or ThoughtWorks.
It is the browser counterpart of lazygocd, a terminal UI for the same problem, and follows its
endpoint choices, which were verified against a production GoCD 23.5.0 instance.

## The problem it solves

GoCD's REST API and its web interface fail independently. The API keeps answering correctly
through server restarts, slow page loads, and a dashboard that loses pipelines; the page in front
of it does not. In production, GoCD's personalized-view lookup has broken and taken the whole web
dashboard down with it while a plain `/api/dashboard` request answered perfectly. GoCD Lens only
uses the API.

## What it does

- Loads every pipeline group, pipeline, pause state and latest run in ONE request to
  `/api/dashboard`, cached to disk so the tab paints instantly and stays readable offline.
- Shows a per-stage status strip on every pipeline card, so you can see which stage broke without
  opening the pipeline.
- Fuzzy search: typing `wabp` finds `web-app-build-prod`, with matched letters highlighted.
- Shows the user's GoCD personalized views, plus two built-in ones (Starred, Watching).
- Per-pipeline detail: paged run history, stages and jobs, manual approval gates marked as gates,
  and the commit, branch, author and message the run was built from.
- Actions: run, pause, resume, stop a running stage, and re-run selected jobs within a stage.
  Each job row carries a checkbox, with failed jobs pre-ticked, so retrying one flaky job does not
  re-run a dozen.
- Console logs tailed live, fetching only new lines, with search, severity colouring, wrapping,
  download and an artifact tree.
- Optional notifications when a watched pipeline starts or finishes, with a bundled chime.
- A toolbar badge counting what is running, turning red with a failure count when nothing is.
- An "is it GoCD, or is it me?" diagnostic that probes the API and the web UI separately.

## Scale and server cost

Designed for large GoCD installations, where a dashboard cannot afford to do work proportional to
the number of pipelines.

- One request per poll regardless of fleet size. No per-pipeline polling exists anywhere.
- Unchanged data costs an empty HTTP 304, because every poll sends the previous ETag.
- A hidden browser tab does not poll at all.
- Several dashboard tabs and the popup share one cache: three open tabs make one request.
- Watching a pipeline adds zero requests; notifications are computed from the dashboard payload
  the badge already needs.
- Background checking when no tab is open ships OFF and must be turned on deliberately.

## Privacy and security facts

- Storage is `chrome.storage.local` only. `chrome.storage.sync`, which would upload to the user's
  Google account, is never used anywhere; a test fails the build if it ever is.
- `host_permissions` in the manifest is an empty list. Access to a single origin is requested with
  `chrome.permissions.request` at the moment the user presses Connect.
- There are NO content scripts, and no `tabs`, `cookies`, `webRequest`, `history` or `scripting`
  permission. The extension cannot read or affect pages the user browses.
- The credential lives only in the background service worker, which makes every request. The
  extension's own pages receive pipeline data only, never the token.
- No remote code, no analytics, no third-party requests. The Content Security Policy blocks inline
  and remote script.
- Three sign-in modes: the existing GoCD browser session (stores nothing at all), a personal
  access token, or HTTP basic auth for older servers. Credentials are verified against the server
  before being saved.
- Build logs, commit messages and pipeline names reach the screen as text nodes. There is no
  `innerHTML` and no `eval` anywhere in the codebase.

## Requirements

Chrome 116 or later; also runs in Microsoft Edge and Brave. Manifest V3. No build step, no server
component, no account, no sign-up.
